$comment: Every user-visible capability, and what actually proves it works.
The distinction this file exists to keep honest: a SHELL journey proves the application starts
and configures itself; a WORKFLOW journey proves a customer got what they came for. Only the
second kind counts as a feature being verified. Unit tests and mock-call assertions never do.
status: green (passing), red (written and failing for a recorded product reason), planned.
A red entry is not a gap in coverage -- it is coverage that has found something.

binary.installed: NSIS setup from --features production, exercised by the isolated installed smoke

journeys.name: startup
journeys.capability: The application launches and renders its editor.
assertions: no error surface is visible with every optional engine absent

journeys.name: defaultFont
journeys.capability: The default subtitle font is installed, verified and drawable on a clean profile.
assertions: native publishes a schema-1 readiness record in state ready with a version
the family measures differently from the generic fallback, so it is not substituted

journeys.name: damagedFontPayload
journeys.capability: A damaged shipped font payload degrades to a typed, actionable state.
fixtures: staged installation copies with a corrupt and a missing font resource
assertions: readiness settles on ready or refused, never waits indefinitely
a refusal carries a bounded token cause, not a path or a message

journeys.name: urlToPreview
journeys.capability: A customer pastes a video URL and gets playable media with a subtitle preview.
fixtures: support/mediaServer.js (loopback HTTP origin with ranges, HEAD, content length)
assertions: the downloader actually requested the fixture from the origin
the activated media is playable and 6 seconds long
no error surface is visible after activation
redReason: On a clean profile the URL workflow first installs its managed downloader tools on demand:
choosing a download type surfaces three 'Cancel installation' controls and the fixture origin
receives zero requests. The download cannot begin until that installation completes, which
needs the network and is not deterministic, so this journey cannot be green offline until the
downloader is a resolved prerequisite rather than an on-demand step during the workflow.

journeys.name: localMediaToPreview
journeys.capability: A customer opens a local video and gets an activated project with a native preview frame.
note: The native dialog is replaced by a staged selection resolved against a declared fixture
root; everything after it -- import, identity, activation, artifacts -- is the real code.
assertions: media activates and the editor shows the source
a native composited frame is published for a cue
the durable project row survives relaunch

journeys.name: subtitlesEditSaveRelaunch
journeys.capability: Subtitles import, edit, history, save and restore across relaunch.

journeys.name: nativeExport
journeys.capability: Native export produces a correct MP4 matching the preview.
oracles: independent ffprobe decode: container, codecs, duration, dimensions
reference pixels compared against captured preview frames

knownProductFindings.finding: First-run onboarding covers every working control in two stages.
detail: A full-screen overlay at z-index 100000 refuses dismissal for four seconds, then a footer
reveal card continues to intercept clicks until 'Let's go' is pressed. Both are intended, but
any automation or accessibility path that does not know about them sees primary controls
reporting as visible and enabled while something else receives the click.

knownProductFindings.finding: The URL workflow installs its downloader during the customer's first attempt.
detail: Pressing Download Only and choosing a type starts managed tool installation rather than a
download. Nothing reaches the origin until it finishes. Worth deciding deliberately: a first
run that needs the network before it can do anything is the same class of problem as the font.

knownProductFindings.finding: Canonicalized media paths were unreadable by Media Foundation.
detail: The storage layer canonicalizes every media location when it records it, which on Windows
returns a verbatim path. MFCreateSourceReaderFromURL reads the leading double backslash as
a network share and fails with ERROR_BAD_NETPATH (0x80070035), so EVERY locally imported
file produced a preview that refused as unreadable, and an export that would have failed
the same way. Measured: the identical bytes probe fine through the plain spelling.
knownProductFindings.fix: osg-decode strips the verbatim prefix for ordinary drive paths in wide_path.

knownProductFindings.finding: No frame decodes when the source height is not a multiple of 16.
detail: Media Foundation reports the unpadded size at open and the macroblock-aligned size once
decoding begins -- 640x360 becomes 640x368 -- and the reader refuses any change as a
mid-stream geometry change. 1080p has the same shape, coding to 1088, so this affects a
large share of ordinary video. Reproduced in a plain unit test, not only through the app.
fix: osg-decode now carries the decoded SURFACE and the VISIBLE picture rectangle separately.
Media Foundation's aperture attributes are read with a documented precedence and each
candidate is validated before use; the reader adopts the decoder's first negotiated output
instead of refusing it, and still refuses a genuine mid-stream change of the picture.

media/bars-6s-640x360.mp4.why: Committed rather than generated: a journey is deterministic only against exact bytes, and a different ffmpeg would silently change what "the 6 second fixture" means.

media/bands-1s-640x360-redfoot.mp4.why: Blue for 352 rows then red for eight, so the rows sitting exactly where macroblock padding would be have a colour of their own. A size check cannot tell padding from picture; this can.

media/bars-1s-1920x1080.mp4.why: 1080 is not a multiple of sixteen, so it decodes into a 1088-row surface: the padded case at the size most real video is.

media/bars-1s-640x360-rotated.mp4.why: Rotation metadata alongside a padded height.

media/bars-1s-640x480-aligned.mp4.why: The control. 480 IS a multiple of sixteen, so no crop applies and a regression that crops always shows up here.

media/bars-1s-720x480-anamorphic.mp4.why: Non-square pixels, so the crop must not disturb the display stretch.
